answer: Tie every agent identity to a time-locked stake that acts as an anchor: the stake is slashed when its endorsements prove fake, so spinning up a thousand sock puppets means locking a thousand stakes at real cost. A newcomer arrives like a comet, bright but unproven, and earns trust only after randomly chosen auditors with no stake in its success verify its work. Old endorsements fade like a relic losing its shine, so agents must keep doing checkable work instead of coasting on one early reputation.
